verdict.reasoning: Patient reports feeling unwell for a few days with cough, cold (nasal symptoms), and sore throat: “I am not feeling very well and I haven't been well for a good few days… I've got a cough, a cold” and later “yeah, yeah, yeah, I've had a bit of a sore throat.”
Patient describes a mostly dry cough worse in the morning: “Yeah, yeah. I mean, mostly dry… In the morning, it's a bit worse. But… it's fairly. Fairly dry.”
Doctor notes runny nose and patient agrees: “I can certainly hear you've got the sniffles. A bit of a runny nose, you mentioned.” Patient: “Yeah, yeah, yeah, I. You're right.”
Patient explicitly reports sore throat: Doctor asks, “any sore throats,” and patient replies, “Yeah, yeah, yeah, I've had a bit of a sore throat.”
Patient links hoarseness to shouting: “I've been shouting myself a wee bit hoarse because the performance has been pretty shy.”

Patient reports some ear-related issue, consistent with mild ear fullness: Doctor asks about “any dullness or blocked ears, pain,” and patient says, “Yeah, yeah, a wee bit… my hearing's… not as good as it used to be, but… I think it's all right.” This supports mild ear symptoms, not severe pain.
Transcript confirms shortness of breath but not limited specifically to exertion: “So you're feeling more short of breath.” Patient: “Yeah.” No exertional context is given.

Patient describes hot and cold sweats: “any… temperatures or fevers, Feeling hot and cold, sweaty?” Patient: “Yeah. Yeah, that's… definitely something I've noticed… get out and get the blanket off and put it back on again.”
Appetite preserved: “And how's your appetite? Are you eating and drinking okay?” Patient: “I think my appetite's been. Been all right. Yeah, yeah. Fluids up as well.”
Single early diarrhea episode: “The first Day I had… a wee bit of diarrhea… but that's. That's fine now and… apart from that, no.”
Symptoms began Saturday, ~5 days prior: Patient and doctor establish it started Saturday and today is Wednesday: “So it would have been Saturday… What's that book? Five. Five days ago.”
Same as cc-001; transcript shows several days of feeling unwell with cough, cold, sore throat: “I haven't been well for a good few days… I've got a cough, a cold” and later sore throat as above.
Patient states type 2 diabetes: “I've got the diabetes.” Doctor: “Diabetes. Right. What type… Type 1 or type 2?” Patient: “It's. It's a type 2.”

Hypertension is confirmed: Patient says a prior doctor took BP and “he said that was, that was high. Higher than it should be.” Doctor clarifies, “You've been diagnosed with high blood pressure or just a one” and patient answers “Yeah,” indicating diagnosis.
Patient self-describes as overweight: “I'm a wee bit on the chunky side… I've got a wee bit around the midriff. The spare tires definitely there.”
Metformin is clearly listed: Patient: “It's metformin.” Doctor: “That's correct.”

A second medication is mentioned but unclear: Patient: “And. And there's another one less lesson.” Doctor attempts to say “Opera. Listen up Real. Yeah, that sounds like.” This supports that a second, unidentified medication exists.

Doctor’s plan: “what we could think about is giving you a… script for antibiotics… which you maybe use the next 24 to 48 hours if your symptoms don't get better… something like amoxicillin, one tablet, three times a day.”
Transcript does not state advice to continue current medications; they are only listed. No recommendation like “continue metformin” is documented.
No allergies reported: Doctor asks, “do you have any allergies at all?” Patient: “Not that I'm aware of… nothing that I'm aware of.”
Patient lives with wife: Doctor: “You said you live with your wife. Anyone else at home with you?” Patient: “No… it's just me and the missus.”
Patient works in a factory: “There’s a wee factory just down the road… we just manufacture like… steel parts… it's a good wee job.”
Alcohol intake: Patient estimates about 9 pints/week mainly weekends: “maybe what, like four. Four pints… Saturday and then… Sunday as well. Maybe like nine. Nine pints in a week.”
Occasional smoking: “What about smoking…?” Patient: “Are we. Every now and again, but I'm. I'm trying to cut that down.”
Vaping to cut down: “I've got a wee… vaporizers… I got myself one of those. So I've been cutting down in the cigarettes and I just got this… wee thing.”
No vitals/physical exam documented; encounter is phone-based, and no measurements or exam maneuvers are mentioned. This absence supports the statement.

Most listed symptoms are documented, but “shortness of breath on exertion” and “mild ear fullness” as exam findings are not. SOB is reported generally (“So you're feeling more short of breath.”), without exertional qualifier, and ear symptoms are historical, not an exam finding. Labeling them as exam findings and specifying exertion adds unsupported detail.
Patient denies chest pain: Doctor: “Any pain in your chest at all?” Patient: “No, no… it's just a wee bit shortness of breath, but it's not pain.”

Only GI symptom is one early diarrhea episode, and no dehydration is described: “The first Day I had… a wee bit of diarrhea… but that's fine now… apart from that, no.” No signs of dehydration are mentioned.
As above, patient explicitly denies chest pain: “Any pain in your chest…?” “No, no… it's not pain.”
Doctor asks about “any nausea, any vomiting, any tummy pain?” Patient: “apart from that, no,” after describing diarrhea, indicating vomiting is denied.
In response to “any… tummy pain?” patient answers “apart from that, no,” denying significant abdominal pain.
Hydration: “And how's your appetite? Are you eating and drinking okay?” Patient: “I think my appetite's been all right. Yeah, yeah. Fluids up as well.”

Doctor’s summary: “what you essentially have is bit of. A. Bit of a viral illness, perhaps a bit of. Maybe early signs of a flu… which I think should settle down…” and acknowledges shortness of breath earlier. This supports viral URI/influenza-like illness with mild dyspnea.
Type 2 diabetes is part of background and relevant to assessment: explicitly diagnosed as type 2 in transcript.
Hypertension is acknowledged as a diagnosed condition (“You've been diagnosed with high blood pressure…” “Yeah”), so including it in assessment is supported.

Overweight and lifestyle risks are described: “wee bit on the chunky side… spare tires,” alcohol intake of ~9 pints/week, and smoking with vaping to cut down. It is reasonable that clinician notes obesity/overweight with these risk factors.
Doctor recommends supportive care: “what you… have is… viral illness… things you can do to help yourself. Stay rested, drink plenty of fluids… taking regular paracetamol would be beneficial.”

Antibiotic plan as stated: “giving you a… script for antibiotics, which you maybe use the next 24 to 48 hours if your symptoms don't get better… something like amoxicillin, one tablet, three times a day.”
There is no explicit instruction to continue diabetes or hypertension medications; current meds are listed but not discussed in the plan.
No mention of planning to review lifestyle risk factors at the next visit appears in the transcript.

Though the doctor encourages quitting (“I wish you all the best in your journey to quit. I highly recommend it”), this is general encouragement, not explicit counseling as part of the plan to continue reducing smoking. The specific phrasing of plan/counseling to continue reduction is not documented.
Hydration and rest are clearly advised: “Stay rested, drink plenty of fluids” and patient repeats “Plenty of rest, lots of water” with doctor agreeing (“Exactly.”).
Alcohol moderation is not discussed in the plan; alcohol use is only quantified, with no counseling to reduce or moderate.

Doctor only states: “Give it about 24 to 40 [48] hours. If you feel like you're still feeling breathless and run down, I think there's no harm in starting a course of antibiotics… And if you're still on better by next week, come back and see me.” There are no instructions specifically tied to worsening SOB, persistent fever, chest symptoms, or no improvement in 24–48 hours beyond starting antibiotics and a general return next week if not better. The detailed set of return precautions is not present.
